''Echeveria sturmiana'' Poelln. }} '''''Echeveria nodulosa''''', the 'painted echeveria', is a species of [[Succulent plant|succulent]] [[flowering plant]] in the [[Crassulaceae]] ([[Sedum|stonecrop]]) family. Fairly popular in cultivation, it is native to [[Mexico]], where it is widely-distributed, and rather common, in northern [[Oaxaca]] and southern [[Puebla]].{{cite web |title=NODULOSA (Baker) Otto, 1873 (engl./ fr.) |url=http://www.crassulaceae.ch/de/artikel?akID=48&aaID=2&aiID=N&aID=230 |access-date=27 November 2017 |website=International Crassulaceae Network}} It is known for its striped, purplish leaves, its "knobby" stems (hence the name ''nodulosa''), and its seasonal display of flowers. They are relatively disease-free, but, like all succulents, may attract [[Scale insect|scale insects]] or [[Mealybug|mealybugs]], which are drawn to the tight crevices and folds between the leaves. If remedied early on, these insects pose no threat to a plant's longevity, though larger, long-term infestations can drain a plant of its vigor and result in death. When in-bloom, the flower buds can sometimes attract [[Aphid|aphids]], which may be difficult to see as they often resemble water droplets on the blossoms.[https://www.gardenia.net/plant/Echeveria-nodulosa-Painted-Echeveria gardenia] Introducing [[Coccinellidae|ladybugs]] may help to counteract aphids, as they are known to readily consume them, especially in the ladybug's larval stages. Pests are easily washed-off with a gentle spray of water or removed by hand, or sprayed with diluted rubbing or [[isopropyl alcohol]], preferably during the early evening; wet leaves exposed to sunlight can cause leaf burn (especially with rubbing alcohol or other chemicals). Additionally, store-bought products, such as [[horticultural oil]] or [[insecticidal soap]], or [[Azadirachta indica|neem]] oil, are effective. == Taxonomy == ''Echeveria'' is named for [[Atanasio Echeverría y Godoy]], a botanical illustrator who contributed to ''Flora Mexicana''.Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback). pp. 149, 274 ''Nodulosa'' means 'with swellings', or 'bearing nodules', and is typically given in reference to the presence of root nodules. ''Echeveria nodulosa'', when compared with other varieties of ''Echeveria'', displays noticeably more "raised" leaf/root nodes along its stems. ==References== {{Reflist}} *[https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/6235/Echeveria-nodulosa/Details RHS.org] {{Taxonbar|from=Q15483198}} [[Category:Endemic flora of Mexico]] [[Category:Echeveria|nodulosa]] [[Category:Taxa named by John Gilbert Baker]] {{Echeveria-stub}}
